title: Extracting the image of a prime divisor without modifying a prescribed open
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $V$ be a normal integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $P$ be a normal integral proper scheme. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $f:V\to P$ be a dominant morphism, meaning that its image is dense. Let $T\subset V$ be an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, meaning $\dim\mathcal O_{V,\eta_T}=1$ at its generic point, where a generic point has closure the whole irreducible closed subset. Let $Z\subsetneq P$ be a closed subset with $f(T)\subseteq Z$. There exist a normal integral proper scheme $P^{\prime}$ and a proper birational morphism $b:P^{\prime}\to P$ which is an isomorphism over $P\setminus Z$. Birational means inducing an isomorphism between dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. The rational lift $f^{\prime}=b^{-1}f$, where rational maps are equivalence classes of morphisms on dense open subschemes, is defined at $\eta_T$. The reduced closure $D=\overline{f^{\prime}(T\cap\operatorname{Dom}(f^{\prime}))}$ is an integral closed subscheme of $b^{-1}(Z)$ with $\dim D=\dim P-1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

proof.text: Put $m=\dim V$, $n=\dim P$, $L=k(V)$ and $K=k(P)$, with function fields the generic stalks. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], nonempty affine charts have these fraction fields. Dominance gives an inclusion $K\subseteq L$ over $k$; affine finite-type presentations make both fields finitely generated over $k$, and hence $L/K$ finitely generated. The schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to the Noetherian field spectrum. By [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr], normality and the specified codimension make $A=\mathcal O_{V,\eta_T}$ a DVR. Use its integer valuation $v:L^\times\to\mathbf Z$ as in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The residue field of $A$ is $k(T)$. The dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k L=m$, $\operatorname{trdeg}_k K=n$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(T)=m-1$. Here every neighbourhood of any point in an integral finite-type scheme has the full dimension, by [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison], so the local topological dimensions in that formula are $m$ and $n$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: Let $p=f(\eta_T)\in Z$. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $p$, the local map $B_{\mathfrak p}\to A$ is injective and local, using the inclusion of function fields from step 1. Since $p$ is not generic, $\mathfrak p\ne0$; choose $0\ne a\in\mathfrak p$. Then $v(a)>0$. Thus $w=v|_{K^\times}$ is nontrivial. Its ring $R=\{0\}\cup\{u\in K^\times:w(u)\ge0\}=A\cap K$ contains $B_{\mathfrak p}$ locally, so gives $c:\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ centred at $p$. Its nonzero value group is a subgroup $e\mathbf Z$ of $\mathbf Z$, $e>0$; choose an element of value $e$. Every nonzero ideal of $R$ has a least occurring nonnegative value, and division by an element of that value expresses it as a principal ideal. Hence $R$ is a local principal ideal domain, not a field, so is a DVR in the sense of [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A\cap K$ and its residue field $\kappa_R$ embeds into $k(T)$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality] to $K\subseteq L$ with valuation ring $A$. Dropping the nonnegative rational-rank term gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa_R}k(T)\le\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$. The tower formula [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower], first for $k\subseteq K\subseteq L$ and then for $k\subseteq\kappa_R\subseteq k(T)$, gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=m-n$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_R\ge(m-1)-(m-n)=n-1$. All quantities in the second tower are finite because $\kappa_R$ embeds into $k(T)$ of finite transcendence degree. Also $n\ge1$: the nongeneric point $p$ has a nonzero prime in a domain chart, so that chart, and hence $P$, has a chain of primes of length one. Choose $n-1$ algebraically independent elements of $\kappa_R$ over $k$ and lifts $h_1,\ldots,h_{n-1}\in R$. If $n=1$, this is the empty list.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-supported-valuation-finite-elements-model] with $X=P$, the closed set $Z$, the centred DVR $R$ and the chosen $h_i$. It gives an integral model $g:Q\to P$ proper and birational, identical over $U=P\setminus Z$, and a lift $c_Q:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Q$. At its centre $q$ all $h_i$ are regular. The model $Q$ is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. In particular it is of finite type over $k$. It has dimension $n$: its function field is $K$, and the generic-point case of [lem-kun-dimension-formula], together with [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison], identifies its dimension with $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text:
Take $
u:P^{\prime}	o Q$ to be the normalization in $K=k(Q)$. The normal integral model is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] with $x=\eta_Q$ and the identity extension $K/\kappa(\eta_Q)$; its stated integral-closure construction is the same normalization. By [lem-sc-normalization-properties], $
u$ is finite birational, $P^{\prime}$ is proper, $\dim P^{\prime}=n$, and $
u$ is an isomorphism over the normal open $g^{-1}U\cong U$. Thus $b=g
u$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], birational and identical over $U$. On the nonempty dense open $f^{-1}U\subseteq V$ there is the prescribed rational lift to $P^{\prime}$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point] over $S=P$ at $\eta_T$, using the DVR $A$, the integral Noetherian source $V$ and the proper target $b$. It extends this lift to an open neighbourhood of $\eta_T$. Denote its value there by $x^{\prime}$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: The two $P$-maps $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Q$ obtained from this extended lift and from $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{c_Q}Q$ agree generically, so are equal by [lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique]; $Q\to P$ is separated because it is proper. Therefore $\nu(x^{\prime})=q$, and the residues of the functions $h_i$ in $\kappa(x^{\prime})$, mapped into $k(T)$, are exactly the independent residues chosen in $\kappa_R$. They are algebraically independent already in $\kappa(x^{\prime})$, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x^{\prime})\ge n-1$. Since $b(x^{\prime})=p\in Z$ and $b$ is dominant, $x^{\prime}$ is nongeneric; its stalk has dimension at least one. By [lem-kun-dimension-formula] and [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison], $n=\dim\mathcal O_{P^{\prime},x^{\prime}}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x^{\prime})$. Hence both bounds are equalities and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x^{\prime})=n-1$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, referring to Milne (2013), Lemma 4.4; valuation/residue proof read at https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2, Lemma 4.4. Supported refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: Every point of $T\cap\operatorname{Dom}(f^{\prime})$ specializes from $\eta_T$, which belongs to this set. Continuity therefore identifies the closure of its image with $\overline{\{x^{\prime}\}}$. Give this irreducible closed subset its reduced induced structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; it is integral, with generic residue field $\kappa(x^{\prime})$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-dimension-comparison] for the integral closed subscheme, the generic-point case of [lem-kun-dimension-formula] identifies its dimension with $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x^{\prime})=n-1$. Finally $b(x^{\prime})\in Z$, and the inverse image of $Z$ is closed, so the entire reduced closure $D$ is contained in $b^{-1}(Z)$.
